name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 18, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:00 p.m., on March 18, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 13, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:03 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Leckness

INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations -- The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are the
  City and the City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg

City Council Minutes  1  March 18, 2013
 CS2. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for closed session item CS1, the Council gave
instruction and provided clarification to staff. This matter will be addressed further as part of the
open session agenda (item 20.) For item CS2, the Council continued its review of the City
Manager but no reportable actions occurred.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Fire Chief Rick Robinson, Battalion Chief Jeff Genoway and Battalion
  Chief Jim Bailey Upon Their Retirement from the Orange County Fire Authority

  Mayor Reardon presented certificates of appreciation to Chiefs Rick Robinson and Jeff
  Genoway. Chief Jim Bailey was unable to attend the meeting.

P2. Presentation by Duane Cave of SDG&E/Sempra Energy

  The City Council received Duane Cave's presentation on the SDG&E/Sempra Energy
  South Orange County Reliability Enhancement project.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Erin Lannon, Sullivan Solar Power: announced that her company is hosting a program to assist
Mission Viejo residents in going solar. The presentation will be held on March 23, 2013, from
11:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. in the Saddleback Room at City Hall. Further information can be found
at www.sullivansolarpower.com.

Tom Glazier, M.V.: announced that the Church of Latter Day Saints will be holding a free
Emergency Preparedness Academy on Saturday, May 4, 2013, from 8:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. and
he invited the City Council Members, staff and residents to attend.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed his attendance at the Orange County Employees
Retirement System (OCERS) Board of Directors meeting where they addressed the
OCFA/OCERS unfunded liability issue. He stated that if contract cities leave OCFA, the
remaining cities will be forced to shoulder the burden and this could threaten Mission Viejo's
reserves.

City Council Minutes  2  March 18, 2013
 Helen Workun, M.V.: announced that she attended Up in the Air at Oso Viejo Park last weekend.
She thanked the City for supporting the Mission Viejo Activities Committee and the MVAC
member/volunteers for their hard work to put on such great shows and activities. Ms. Workun
encouraged residents to attend next year and she noted that Susan Brown Matsumi made a nice
video on the event which can be found on YouTube.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: reiterated compliments on Up In the Air and announced that there is a
great video on the MVAC Facebook page that captured the event from the air. She outlined her
attendance at the Wounded Warriors Amputee Softball game and offered her thanks to the small
team of volunteers who organize that event for a very good cause. Mrs. Bucknum announced that
the upcoming television show Splash will feature our own Mission Viejo Nadadores divers and
she thanked Mayor Reardon and Council Member Leckness for attending the recent San Diego
Water Board hearing on the 241 Tesoro extension completion. Lastly, she encouraged parents to
sign up and attend the Sheriff Department's Parent Project program to understand what kids are
facing in our schools.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 6 and 7 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for regular City Council meeting of March 4, 2013, as presented.

3.  Check Register Dated February 22, 2013 in the Amount of $1,058,014.79

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated March 1, 2013 in the Amount of $593,089.11

City Council Minutes  3  March 18, 2013
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Fifth Amendment to the Mission Viejo Library’s Technical Services Outsourcing
  Agreement for Purchase of New Library Books

  Approved the Fifth Amendment to the City of Mission Viejo Technical Services
  Outsourcing Agreement with Baker & Taylor, Inc., and increased the purchase order in an
  amount not to exceed $30,000, for a total of $165,000 for the total term of the two-year
  Agreement.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for January 2013

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January
  2013

  Received and filed.

10. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for January 2013

  Received and filed.

11. La Paz Road Median Island Runoff Prevention Project

  Adopted Resolution No. 13-17 Amending the Fiscal Year 2012-2013 Budget to Create
  Capital Improvement Project 216 to Construct the La Paz Road Median Island Runoff
  Prevention Project.

12. Oso Parkway Widening, I-5 to Country Club Drive (CIP 791)-Grant Funding
  Extension

  Adopted Resolution 13-18 Authorizing the City Manager to Request an Extension of Time
  from the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) for Funding for the Oso
  Parkway Widening, Country Club Drive to Interstate 5 Freeway (CIP 791.)

13. La Paz Bridge and Road Widening, Muirlands to Chrisanta (CIP 756/761)-Grant
  Funding Extension

  Adopted Resolution 13-19 Authorizing the City Manager to Request an Extension of Time
  from the Orange County Transportation Authority for Funding for the La Paz Bridge and
  Road Widening Project (CIP 756/761).

City Council Minutes  4  March 18, 2013
 PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

14. Termination of Inclusionary Housing Agreement and Acknowledgement of Park Fee
  Obligation ("Termination Agreement") between Mission Viejo Housing Authority
  and Mission Viejo Oso Parkway Development, LP, a California limited partnership,
  relating to the Andalucia Mission Viejo Apartments

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report on behalf of Special Counsel Celeste
  Brady.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she will be voting no on this item as a protest because
  she believes that the matter was handled unprofessionally.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve
  Termination of Inclusionary Housing Agreement (A13-06) and Acknowledgement of Park
  Fee Obligation for Andalucia Mission Viejo Apartments.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

6.  Youth Services Program Contract Amendment

  Council Member Schlicht asked how or when the City can take care of possibly increasing
  the rate that the parents are paying for the Kids Factory program.

  City Manager Wilberg noted that during the upcoming budget development, staff will look
  at ways to reduce costs and/or increase fees.

  Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: asked the Council to think of this program along the lines of
  public safety. If families can't afford to utilize the program it won't work however, she
  agrees that it does need to be evaluated.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to amend the
  contract with the Saddleback Valley Unified School District (SVUSD) Department of
  Recreation and Community Services to provide Youth Services Programs through Fiscal
  Year 2012-13 in the amount of $760,000.
City Council Minutes  5  March 18, 2013
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

7.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2013

  Mayor Reardon asked Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas to explain the
  uneven cash flow concept.

  Director Dyas outlined the property tax and sales tax receipt dates which can cause a
  significant difference between inflows and outflows in any given month.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to receive and
  file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

15. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: continued his comments from earlier in the evening regarding
  the recent OCERS Board Meeting and he asked what Mission Viejo's unfunded liability
  would be, relative to its contract with OCFA. He also expressed his support for the OCFA
  Board's direction to staff to study its procurement system.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

16. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

17. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

18. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.
City Council Minutes  6  March 18, 2013
 19. SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that she was unable to attend last SCAG TCC meeting
  but she provided the brief update that she received on the meeting.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

20. Revisions to the City of Mission Viejo Flexible Benefit Plans and Fixed Monthly City
  Contribution Schedule

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 13-20 Revising the City's Retiree Insurances Program effective March 18, 2013.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 13-21 Revising the City's Flexible Benefit Plans and Fixed Monthly
  Contribution Schedule effective April 1, 2013 (as reflected in Exhibit B.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to table item 3
  in the recommended action until staff finishes with the procurement of a new financial
  management system.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Manager Wilberg announced that he will be passing out a master schedule of the
maintenance contracts that will be coming before the Council in the next 2 months.
City Council Minutes  7  March 18, 2013
 City Attorney’s Report

21. Request Made by the Mission Viejo Family YMCA for an Exemption to the "No
  Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation

  At the hour of 7:59 p.m., Mayor Reardon announced that she will vacate the room and will
  not participate in this matter due to her position on the YMCA Board of Directors. At that
  time, Mayor Pro Tem Kelley assumed control of the meeting.

  City Manager Wilberg drew the Council's attention to a typo in the recommended action
  which refers to the Marguerite Aquatics Center. He noted that it should read the Marguerite
  Recreation Center.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve
  the request made by the Mission Viejo Family YMCA for an exemption to the "No
  Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" at the Marguerite Aquatics Center.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Reardon

  Mayor Reardon returned to the dais at 8:01 p.m.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

22. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness announced that he would like to show a preview of the new television
show, Splash. Because the video was not ready, he asked Mayor Reardon to come back to him
after the other Council Members have shared their comments.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that the health care vote was a tough one for her because she
was weighing the employees' needs with the City Council's ability to control costs and she is
conflicted about the outcome. She outlined her attendance at the Wounded Warriors softball
game and she stated that these marvelous men are a testament to Americans and they are

City Council Minutes  8  March 18, 2013
 continuing to give back to the community. Although she couldn't attend this year's Up in the Air
event, Council Member Schlicht noted that she has enjoyed it in past years. She also discussed
her attendance at Senator Mark Wyland's Inaugural Orange County Albondigas event and she
recommended that residents attend the upcoming Saddleback Republican Assembly Meeting to
hear Daniel Chen, author of My Grandfather's America. That meeting will be held at 7:00 p.m.
on Thursday, March 21, 2013, at the Murray Community Center. Council Member Schlicht
wished everyone Passover greetings and happy Easter and she concluded with two quotes from
G.K. Chesterton: "The most astonishing thing about miracles is that they happen," and in honor
of the Wounded Warriors: "The true solider fights not because he hates what is in front of him
but because he loves what is behind him."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury outlined his attendance at a recent ACC-OC meeting on fire prevention
and technologies. It turned out to be a fantastic 2-hour discussion on new technologies in
firefighting which are driving down the costs of firefighting and damage repair. Council Member
Ury noted that it was an extremely informative and dynamic program and he will be sharing
copies of the tape with his colleagues.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that she has been helping her daughter who recently had her
third baby so she has been a little bit out of the loop. She did however attend the Wounded
Warriors Softball Game. She enjoyed the teaching opportunity with her 2 year-old and 4 year-old
grandsons and she was able to explain to them that these men are real life heroes. Mayor Pro
Tem Kelley stated that it is hard for young children to wrap their arms around that but they did a
pretty good job of understanding that these men went off to fight the "bad guys" and were hurt
while protecting our country. She noted that it gave her a grateful heart and greater appreciation
for the price that our service men and women pay to keep this the land of the free and the home
of the brave.

Council Member Leckness (Continued)

Council Member Leckness shared a preview of the new television show Splash which will begin
airing on Tuesday, March 19, 2013. He announced that eight of the eleven divers are from our
own Nadadores team and have trained with the celebrities here in Mission Viejo.

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon outlined her attendance at the Mayor's Prayer Breakfast with keynote speaker
Steve Scheibner. Mr. Scheibner was the pilot who, after a series of events, was bumped from
Flight 11 on September 11, 2001. Mayor Reardon announced that Council Member Ury has been
elected to First Vice President of the ACC-OC and will be ascending to the role of President next
year. She also discussed her attendance at the ACC-OC presentation on fire metrics and she
agreed with Council Member Ury that it was well worth their time. She also noted that she and
City Council Minutes  9  March 18, 2013
 City Manager Dennis Wilberg had a productive meeting with Senator Mark Wyland last week.
Mayor Reardon read an email from a resident who was unable to attend the meeting but wanted
to give the City kudos for the Wounded Warriors event. She also read a note from retiring
firefighter Dave Hahn who expressed his thanks to those who serve the City for building the
foundation for a family oriented community that is second to none. Lastly, Mayor Reardon noted
that this is a sacred time of year and she wished residents a very nice Easter.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:19 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting to Monday, April 1, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 1, 2013

City Council Minutes  10  March 18, 2013
